record.paper_title: Open Problems in α Particle Condensation
record.original_question: In neutron-rich linear-chain nuclei such as ¹⁶C, do extra neutrons stabilize α-chain geometries while partly or completely preventing α condensation among the α clusters?

evidence.quote: The linear chain structures probably are strongly stabilized if a couple of neutrons are added. Actually the linear chain has recently be considered by Itagaki et al. in 16C [26].

In such a case, it would be extremely interesting whether the fact that extra neutrons are between three α’s hinders condensation to be born out to some extent or even totally, see also discussion in Sec. 4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a neutron-rich light nucleus modeled as a linear chain of three α-particles (each α being a tightly bound ⁴He cluster) together with a small number of extra valence neutrons placed between or around the α clusters; the canonical example is ¹⁶C, viewed as a 3α+4n system in a linear-chain geometry. By "α condensation" we mean a state in which all α clusters occupy a common 0S center-of-mass orbit of a self-consistent mean field (an α-particle Bose–Einstein-condensate-like state, generalizing the Hoyle-state picture of ¹²C), characterized by a large occupation of the lowest 0S single-α orbital in the bosonic α-density matrix.

Question: In such neutron-rich linear-chain nuclei, do the extra valence neutrons (i) stabilize the linear α-chain geometry against bending and breakup, while simultaneously (ii) partially or completely suppress α-particle condensation among the three α clusters (i.e., reduce the occupation of the 0S α-orbital so that the state ceases to be an α condensate)?

Make this precise by determining, for the ground or low-lying 0⁺ linear-chain states of 3α+Nn systems (N = 2, 4, ...), both the binding/stability of the chain configuration and the bosonic α-occupation numbers, and decide whether in the limit of added neutrons the α-condensate fraction is reduced and, if so, to what extent.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent works (Itagaki et al.; AMD studies of ¹⁶C; covariant density functional and Skyrme mean-field calculations; studies of 5α in ²⁰Ne) confirm that extra neutrons can stabilize linear α-chain configurations in neutron-rich C isotopes, particularly under rotation, but a definitive quantitative determination of whether the extra neutrons partially or fully suppress α-particle condensation among the α clusters has not been settled. The question of how valence neutrons affect the α-condensate fraction in linear-chain nuclei remains an active open problem.

status_evidence.title: Linear-chain structure of three α-clusters in 16C and 20C
status_evidence.snippet: Skyrme mean-field investigation of linear-chain configurations of three α-clusters with four or eight valence neutrons in 16C and 20C, discussing stability versus neutron number.
status_evidence.claim: Extra neutrons are studied as a stabilizing factor for 3α linear chains.

status_evidence.title: Effects of rotation and valence nucleons in molecular α-chain nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: σ orbitals occupied by valence neutrons lower in energy with rotational frequency, indicating linear-chain cluster structures are more feasible in fast-rotating neutron-rich nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: Valence neutrons help stabilize α-chain structures, but the impact on α-condensation is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: 3α clustering in the excited states of 16C
status_evidence.snippet: Two types of α-cluster states in 16C: triangular and linear-chain, with valence neutrons in sd and pf orbitals.
status_evidence.claim: Linear-chain 3α states with extra neutrons exist in 16C; their condensate character is still under investigation.
